title: Nested Control Flow
definition: Nested control flow places a decision or repetition structure inside another structure so that the inner behavior is reached only through the enclosing path.
purpose: Represent composite decisions and repeated dimensions while keeping the complete execution path traceable.
history: Structured programming established sequence, selection, and iteration as composable control structures.
mental_model: Treat each opening structure as entering a room: the inner room can be reached only after every outer door on that path has opened.
analogy: A building floor and room number form two dimensions; the analogy fails when program state changes between visits.
common_mistakes: Losing track of state inside nesting
industry_notes: Nesting is not inherently incorrect, but deep and interacting nesting raises review and change cost.
ai_notes: Require AI-generated nested flow to include a path list, state trace, and boundary tests.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to trace one path and explain which outer conditions make it reachable.
